Channels in Go are typed conduits for passing values between goroutines. Unbuffered channels block the sender until a receiver is ready. Buffered channels block only when the buffer is full.
sync.Mutex protects shared state. Lock before access, unlock after. Use defer mu.Unlock() immediately after mu.Lock() to avoid forgetting unlock on early returns or panics.

Deadlocks occur when goroutines wait indefinitely. Common causes: circular lock ordering, unbuffered channel sends without receivers, forgetting to unlock mutexes, and recursive mutex locking (sync.Mutex is not reentrant).
Go's race detector (go run -race) identifies concurrent memory access bugs. It instruments memory accesses at runtime and reports conflicting accesses. Use it during testing and CI.

context.Context carries deadlines, cancellation signals, and request-scoped values. Pass it as the first parameter to functions that span multiple goroutines or do I/O. Derive child contexts with context.WithTimeout or context.WithCancel.

Go's GC is concurrent and non-generational by default. GOGC controls the target heap size percentage. Lower GOGC means more frequent but smaller GC pauses. Use runtime/debug.SetGCPercent to tune at runtime.
sync.Map is optimized for either read-heavy workloads or when keys are only written once. It is not a drop-in replacement for a regular map in write-heavy scenarios.

The channel owner goroutine pattern serializes access to a shared resource through a single goroutine that owns the data. Other goroutines send requests on a request channel and receive responses on a response channel.
sync/atomic provides low-level atomic memory operations like AddInt64, CompareAndSwapInt32, LoadPointer. Use them for simple counters and flags. Do not use them for complex state transitions.
fmt.Errorf with %%w wraps an error so errors.Is and errors.As can inspect the chain. Wrap errors as they propagate up the call stack to preserve the original cause and add operational context.

Standard Go project layout: /cmd for application entry points, /internal for private application code, /pkg for reusable libraries, /api for OpenAPI specs, /configs for configuration files, /docs for documentation, /scripts for CI/build scripts.

Go modules (go.mod) define the module path, Go version, and dependencies. go.sum stores cryptographic hashes of dependencies. The module cache is in GOPATH/pkg/mod. Use 'go mod tidy' to clean up dependencies.

Go interfaces should be defined by the consumer, not the producer. Keep interfaces small (1-3 methods). Accept interfaces, return concrete structs. This enables mocking and prevents unnecessary coupling.

Table-driven tests use a slice of test cases and t.Run for subtests. Use testify/assert or the standard testing package. For benchmarks, use testing.B with b.ReportAllocs(). Example tests go in _test.go files in the same package.

Goroutine leaks happen when goroutines block forever on channel operations or never exit. Use context.Context for cancellation, close channels to signal completion, and profile goroutines with runtime/pprof or go tool pprof goroutine.

select lets a goroutine wait on multiple channel operations. Use it with a default case for non-blocking sends/receives, or with context.Done() for cancellation. Always include a default case in loops to avoid blocking.

Pipeline pattern chains stages via channels. Each stage is a goroutine that receives from an input channel, processes, and sends to an output channel. Close channels when done. Use waitgroups to coordinate stage shutdown.
defer schedules a function call to run when the surrounding function returns. Use it for cleanup: unlocking mutexes, closing files, releasing network connections. Deferred calls run in LIFO order.
